summary: Fixed at the source on the Dart display side and hardened on the Rust side; ONE production writer of the fabricated (0,0) survives in a file outside ownership (see needs_shared_change). New packages/skotiq_app/lib/services/observing_site.dart makes 'no observing site on record' a first-class ABSENT value: observingSiteProvider (LocationSettings?), siteTwilightTimesProvider (TwilightTimes?) and siteMoonTimesProvider (MoonTimes?) return null when there is no site, so a consumer has nothing to render rather than a Null Island night. All four remaining ungated consumers now route through it - cockpit_sky_context.dart (dark window + 'Astro dark left' countdown), command_bar.dart NightContextChip (self-hides, divider included), standby/night_timeline.dart (painted band + IMAGING WINDOW + moon markers), planetarium/tonight_tab.dart (twilight cards, darkness card, moonrise/moonset, target ranking, satellite passes, and the printed coordinates). The two per-surface `lat == 0.0 && lon == 0.0` sentinels that had been added to night_timeline.dart and command_bar.dart are DELETED, not relocated - the item is right that (0,0) is a real place. Rust half: state.rs no longer fabricates the ABSENCE of a site either. get_observer_location used to answer Ok(None) whenever a writer held the tokio lock, which is indistinguishable from 'this user has no site' to polar alignment's refusal-to-run, the sequencer's meridian maths and the FITS SITELAT/SITELONG writer - and the settings fan-out puts a writer there at exactly the moment surfaces first ask. The field is now a std::sync::RwLock (which also removes the blocking_write() panic hazard the old write path had on async callers) and load_observer_location_from_settings loads absence as absence instead of skipping the write. state.rs itself never fabricated (0,0): AppSettings.location is already Option<ObserverLocation> and api_set_location already takes Option, so there is no honest change left to make there.
test: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test --package skotiq_bridge --lib  (465 passed, 0 failed)
revert_check: SIX severs, each at a PRODUCTION call site, each restored and re-verified green. (1) cockpit_sky_context.dart:39 `ref.watch(siteTwilightTimesProvider)` -> `ref.watch(twilightTimesProvider)`: 2 failures ('idle asks for a location instead of naming a dark window', 'with a target, "astro dark left" is blank without a site'). (2) command_bar.dart:560 same substitution: 1 failure ('NightContextChip self-hides entirely when no site is on record'). (3) night_timeline.dart:29-30 `siteTwilightTimesProvider`/`siteMoonTimesProvider` -> `twilightTimesProvider`/`moonInfoProvider`: 1 failure ('NightTimeline says nothing about the night when no site is on record'). (4) tonight_tab.dart:86-87 same substitution: 1 failure ('TonightTab prompts for a location instead of a Null Island night'). (5) the shared gate itself - deleted `if (ref.watch(observingSiteProvider) == null) return null;` from BOTH siteTwilightTimesProvider and siteMoonTimesProvider in observing_site.dart: 6 of 11 failed. (6) RUST: in state.rs get_observer_location, replaced `let location = self.read_observer_location().clone();` with the old `self.observer_location.try_read().map(|g| g.clone()).unwrap_or(None)` -> state::tests::a_busy_lock_never_reports_the_site_as_unset FAILED at state.rs:787 ('a held write lock is not the user has no site'); restored -> 3 passed. Every sever cut the WIRING in the widget's build method, not a helper, and the gating test pumps the real production widgets.
caveats: 1) The 4 failures in test/screens/dashboard/captures_landscape_test.dart are PRE-EXISTING golden-image mismatches (~40% pixel diff; Windows-captured goldens on Linux). Proven, not assumed: I swapped all four owned widgets back to their HEAD content and removed observing_site.dart, re-ran, and got the identical 4 failures. Files restored immediately afterwards and the suite re-run. 2) The Rust lock change is a type change on AppState.observer_location (tokio RwLock -> std::sync::RwLock); all 465 bridge lib tests pass, but it has not been exercised on hardware. 3) The moon's PHASE and ILLUMINATION are deliberately still shown with no site - they are the same everywhere on Earth. Only rise/set are gated. 4) Not verified in a running GUI, only in widget tests.
needs_shared_change: The app STILL writes a fabricated site into the native store on every launch; the display surfaces just no longer repeat it. packages/skotiq_app/lib/services/location_sync_service.dart (outside ownership) is the sole production writer. Its `ref.listen(appSettingsProvider, ...)` branch calls `_syncLocationToBackend(ref, settings.latitude, settings.longitude, settings.elevation)` UNCONDITIONALLY, and AppSettingsState.latitude/longitude/elevation are non-nullable doubles defaulting to 0.0 (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_sections/app_settings_state.dart:21-23, 477-479). That is the `Setting observer location: lat=0, lon=0, elev=0` line in the log. Note the file's own initial-read branch a few lines below already guards with `if (settings.latitude != 0.0 || settings.longitude != 0.0)`, so the two paths disagree - the listen path wins at startup. FIX: in the listen branch, pass ABSENCE as absence. No signature change is needed anywhere - ProfileSettingsBackend.setLocation already takes `models.ObserverLocation?` (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/roles/profile_settings_backend.dart:50) and api_set_location already takes `Option<ObserverLocation>` (bridge/src/api/storage.rs:163). Feed it `ref.read(appObserverLocationProvider)` mapped to ObserverLocation-or-null rather than the raw settings triple. This matters beyond cosmetics: a Some() in native state is what polar alignment, the sequencer's altitude/meridian maths and the FITS SITELAT/SITELONG writer all branch on, and set_observer_location PERSISTS, so one bad write outlives the launch that made it. SECOND, deeper change: appObserverLocationProvider (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_provider.dart:208-232) currently derives 'no site' from exactly the `latitude == 0.0 && longitude == 0.0` sentinel this item forbids. It is the single place the sentinel now lives, and every gate in this fix ultimately rests on it, so an observer genuinely at 0/0 is told they have no site. The structural fix is for AppSettingsState to carry a nullable `LocationSettings?` instead of three non-nullable doubles, sourced from the Rust AppSettings.location which is ALREADY Option<ObserverLocation> and already models absence correctly - the flattening happens on the Dart side. That touches the settings model, its persistence, onboarding and every settings surface, which is why it is called out rather than done here. Two sequencer call sites (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor.dart:1736 and .../sequence_executor/runtime_config_operations.dart:20) also use the sentinel, but they SKIP rather than write, so they do not fabricate - they only fail to clear a site fabricated earlier, which the location_sync_service fix resolves.
